title: Only the file you meant
description:
Check plug-in paths before loading them.

```
plugins\fire.dll        -> refused: relative path
C:\Game\plugins\fire.dll -> ok
C:\Game\plugins\..\..\Windows\evil.dll -> refused: leaves the plugin folder
C:\Game\plugins\notes.txt -> refused: not a .dll
```
hints: Two `fs::path` members do the path work. `p.is_absolute()` is true for a full path such as `C:\Game\plugins\fire.dll` and false for `plugins\fire.dll`. `p.lexically_normal()` returns a cleaned-up copy, dropping `.` parts and letting each `..` cancel the part before it, without touching the disk: `fs::path{ "C:\\Game\\plugins\\..\\x.dll" }.lexically_normal()` is `C:\Game\x.dll`.

After normalising, compare text as in lesson 4.02's practice: the candidate's `.string()` must begin with the plugin folder's `.string()` followed by a backslash (`text.compare(0, prefix.size(), prefix) == 0` tests how a string begins). `extension()` gives `.dll`; lower-case it before comparing.
On Linux the backslashes are not separators; write the tests with `/` there, or build paths with `/` operators.
requirements: Refuse a relative path, then use `std::filesystem::path` to normalise the candidate (`lexically_normal`, see the hints) before checking it.
The result must be inside the allowed plugin folder and end in `.dll` (any case).
Print the reason for each refusal.
stretch: Also check that the file is signed (described in a comment: `WinVerifyTrust`).
